claims.text: Adding 2–5 at.% Al to CoCrFeMnNi alters elemental partitioning and local chemical ordering.
Adding 2–5 at.% Al increases the thermodynamic driving force for formation of protective Al2O3.
Al-induced partitioning and chemical ordering facilitate formation of a continuous Al2O3-enriched passive film.
The Al2O3-enriched passive film is chemically inert, adherent, and mechanically robust.
The Al2O3-enriched film is more resistant to mechanical removal during sliding wear.
The Al2O3-enriched film is more resistant to accelerated corrosion.
Improved film resistance reduces synergistic wear-corrosion damage.
Al doping reduces pit initiation under simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Al doping reduces wear-track propagation under simultaneous wear and corrosion.
The Al-doped alloy will have lower cumulative mass loss than undoped CoCrFeMnNi under combined wear-corrosion conditions.
The Al-doped alloy will have lower pit density and pit depth than undoped CoCrFeMnNi under combined wear-corrosion conditions.
The Al-doped alloy will have shallower wear tracks than undoped CoCrFeMnNi under combined wear-corrosion conditions.
Undoped CoCrFeMnNi forms an oxide that is less robust and more mechanically vulnerable than the film on the Al-doped alloy.
The predicted protective mechanism requires sufficiently high oxygen levels and moderate chloride concentrations.
The protective mechanism may fail under extremely low oxygen conditions.
The protective mechanism may fail when mechanical stress exceeds the protective capability of the Al2O3-enriched film.
